#!/bin/bash
# check_mount_latency.sh - time a stat() on every mount from /proc/mounts.
set -uo pipefail
CRIT="${1:-5}"
worst=0; worst_m=""; out=()
while read -r _ m fstype _; do
  case "$fstype" in proc|sysfs|tmpfs|devtmpfs|cgroup2) continue ;; esac
  # autofs indirect maps: stat() triggers a mount and measures the automounter, not NFS.
  [[ "$fstype" == autofs ]] && continue
  t=$( { /usr/bin/time -f %e stat -t "$m" >/dev/null; } 2>&1 )
  out+=("$m $t s")
  if (( $(echo "$t > $worst" | bc) )); then worst=$t; worst_m=$m; fi
done < /proc/mounts
if (( $(echo "$worst > $CRIT" | bc) )); then
  echo "MOUNT CRITICAL - $worst_m stat() took $worst s (crit $CRIT s); ${out[*]}"; exit 2
fi
echo "MOUNT OK - ${out[*]}"; exit 0

answer:
It is the same false positive, and the fix never reached this check.

- Icinga: `mount-latency` is CRITICAL since 2026-11-17 01:40 UTC: "/home/autofs/proj stat() took 12.4 s (crit 5 s)",
  while /home/users (0.02 s) and /srv/scratch (0.03 s) are fast. The service's vars set plugin =
  plugins/fs/check_mount_latency.sh and plugin_ref = v3.4.0.
- Comments: hkowalczyk wrote on 2026-11-15 14:20 UTC that the autofs false positive was fixed in the plugin on main
  (it now skips autofs entries). Since then, amensah commented on 2026-11-17 08:05 UTC that it came back overnight on
  the same mount, with users reporting no slowness on /home/users.
- GitHub: on main the plugin does skip autofs (`[[ "$fstype" == autofs ]] && continue`). At tag v3.4.0 - the ref this
  service is pinned to - there is no autofs skip, so it still stat()s the autofs indirect mount and times the
  automounter.

So the fix exists only on main; the check still runs the v3.4.0 plugin, which does not contain it. The 12.4 s is the
automounter on /home/autofs/proj, not NFS latency. To make the fix stick, move plugin_ref to a release that contains the
autofs skip (or to main). The host-level comment about the 2026-11-25 kernel rollout is unrelated.
